job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today our school visited a local forest reserve. Our teacher explained that 'Reserved Forests' are the most valuable category, managed by the state to protect timber and wildlife, not just for government officials. We also learned about the Bishnoi community’s role in protecting sacred groves. These groves are not just for medicinal plants; they are patches of forest held in high esteem by local communities, often dedicated to local deities, ensuring the protection of the entire ecosystem. Finally, we discussed Project Tiger. It is a massive conservation effort that goes beyond just stopping hunting; it focuses on habitat restoration and maintaining the ecological balance required for the tiger's survival. It is fascinating to see how conservation is a collective effort involving both the government and local people, rather than just a top-down approach. Understanding these classifications and community efforts has completely changed how I view our natural heritage. I feel more responsible for protecting our environment now.

items.evidence: Our teacher explained that 'Reserved Forests' are the most valuable category, managed by the state to protect timber and wildlife, not just for government officials.
items.q: What is the main purpose of keeping an area as a Reserved Forest?
options: To guard its timber and wild animals
To give officials a private place to visit
To leave it unsurveyed for later discovery
To grow medicinal plants for local deities
items.explain: The state manages Reserved Forests to protect timber and wildlife, not just for government officials.

wrong.why: thinks reserved forests are only for officials
confuses forest categories with unsurveyed land
mixes in details about sacred groves

items.evidence: These groves are not just for medicinal plants; they are patches of forest held in high esteem by local communities, often dedicated to local deities, ensuring the protection of the entire ecosystem.
items.q: Why do communities protect the whole sacred grove, not just a few useful plants?
options: It is honoured and often devoted to local gods
It is valued only for its rare medicinal plants
It is a Reserved Forest run by the state
It is saved only where the government pays
items.explain: Communities respect sacred groves and dedicate them to deities, so the entire ecosystem is protected.

wrong.why: thinks groves matter only for medicinal plants
mixes up sacred groves with reserved forests
thinks community conservation needs government money

items.evidence: It is a massive conservation effort that goes beyond just stopping hunting; it focuses on habitat restoration and maintaining the ecological balance required for the tiger's survival.
items.q: Suppose all tiger hunting has stopped. What work would Project Tiger still need to do?
options: Restoring habitats and keeping nature in balance
Only watching that hunters never come back
Reducing tiger numbers, as the British planned
Saving medicinal plants in the sacred groves
items.explain: Project Tiger goes beyond stopping hunting; it restores habitats and keeps the ecological balance tigers need.

wrong.why: thinks Project Tiger is only about hunting
thinks the British started it to control tigers
picks a nearby detail from the passage

items.evidence: It is fascinating to see how conservation is a collective effort involving both the government and local people, rather than just a top-down approach.
items.q: Which example best matches the writer's view of how conservation should work?
options: Villagers and forest officials guarding a forest together
Officials alone enforcing strict rules on villagers
Villagers acting only when the government funds them
Forest guards stopping hunters and doing nothing else
items.explain: The writer says conservation is a joint effort of government and local people, not top-down.

wrong.why: picks the top-down approach the writer rejects
thinks community efforts need government funding
thinks wildlife loss comes only from hunting
